title: Synthetic response paths
caption: Figure 1. Six known mechanisms and their estimated responses. Shading is an event wild-bootstrap simultaneous band across 20 horizons; these are simulated data.

title: Coverage audit
caption: Figure 2. Accepted event windows divided by planned events. Every required minute from −61 to +25 must be present and valid; missing bars are never filled.

title: Primary response across samples
caption: Figure 3. SPX provider-quote response to the frozen rate-surprise factor after clock correction. Pooled estimates are retrospective. Chronological transfer follows a documented source-clock repair after the original holdout had been examined; sample eligibility is reported separately.

title: Assets and communication types
caption: Figure 4. Pooled response curves with pointwise HC3 intervals. Panels have independent vertical scales. Asset and event-type comparisons are exploratory; the factor remains scaled to development statements.

title: Lagged response estimates
caption: Figure 5. The additional 5-to-20-minute response and its 95% HC3 interval. An interval containing zero does not establish that adjustment is complete.

title: External window cross-check
caption: Figure 6. The same nominal −10-to-+20-minute window compared with USMPD stock-index and futures returns. Agreement supports alignment; different instruments, quote conventions and boundary sampling prevent treating it as minute-level ground truth.

title: Event activity and matched days
caption: Figure 7. First-20-minute realised variance relative to the matched weekday. Intervals are event-pair bootstrap intervals; a variance increase measures activity rather than the fraction of information absorbed.

title: Chronological prediction check
caption: Figure 8. Frozen corrected-development predictions on later statements. Negative differences favour the surprise model. This post-audit transfer follows the A02 clock repair, not an untouched holdout; within-window inputs are retrospective and +20-minute publication latency is not modelled.

title: Lead–lag diagnostics
caption: Figure 9. Pooled within-event minute-return correlations. A peak at zero is common co-movement; a nonzero-lag peak can also reflect quote timing or shared news and does not establish causation.

title: Influence of individual events
caption: Figure 10. The pooled SPX 20-minute slope after omitting each accepted statement in turn. This evaluates event influence without removing inconvenient observations from the main estimate.

title: Sequential information releases
caption: Figure 11. The first later-period statement, selected by date. The subsequent press conference introduces additional information; movements after that release cannot be attributed solely to delayed incorporation of the statement.

title: Clock-audit evidence
caption: Figure 12. Independent download routes show that the documented clock misaligns the two series. Correcting the seasonal offset raises their minute-return correlation from −0.004 to 0.9995 on this probe. This checks timing rather than proving source independence or universal data quality.
